claims.claim: The tool installs nothing: it runs on the Python standard library alone.
claims.method: the package imports only json, argparse, subprocess, pathlib, re, time; pyproject declares an empty dependency list

claims.claim: The CLI exposes run, check, list, coverage and index.

check.cmd: python3 -m verify_claims --help; python3 -m verify_claims run --help; python3 -m verify_claims coverage --help; python3 -m verify_claims index --help

claims.claim: The version the package reports equals the version in pyproject.toml.

cmd: python3 -c "import tomllib,pathlib; print('manifest', tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']['version'])" 2>/dev/null || python3 -c "import re,pathlib; print('manifest', re.search(r'^version = \"([^\"]+)\"', pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text(), re.M).group(1))"

claims.claim: The example repository's claims all reproduce.
claims.metric: counts printed by a run over example/
claims.method: the example reads example/data.json and prints its numbers; the claims file asserts that output

claims.claim: Strict mode turns a manual (unchecked) claim into a failed run.
claims.method: the example carries one claim that no command can check; --strict must reject it
claims.repro: python3 -m verify_claims --root example run --strict; echo exit=$?

check.cmd: python3 -m verify_claims --root example run --strict >/dev/null 2>&1; echo exit=$?

claims.claim: A claim with neither a command nor a written reason is refused, and the tool refuses to run such a file.
claims.method: tests/fixtures/invalid/claims.json omits the check block on purpose
claims.repro: python3 -m verify_claims --root tests/fixtures/invalid check; python3 -m verify_claims --root tests/fixtures/invalid run; echo exit=$?

check.cmd: python3 -m verify_claims --root tests/fixtures/invalid run >/dev/null 2>&1; echo exit=$?

claims.metric: tests reported by the standard-library runner

check.cmd: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | grep -o '^Ran [0-9]* tests'

claims.claim: docs/case-studies.md documents six failure modes (plus the section on wrongly written checks).
claims.method: the document groups the audited failures by mode; this claim keeps the count honest

claims.claim: docs/measurement.md's per-repo table sums to its own stated totals: 16 repositories, 553 claims checked, 98 contradicted, 33 unsupported, 131 defective (24%).
claims.metric: the table's rows summed and compared with the total row, in the document itself
claims.method: the audit's per-repo verdicts were recorded per batch; this keeps the report's arithmetic honest if either the rows or the totals are edited

check.cmd: python3 -c "import re,pathlib;t=pathlib.Path('docs/measurement.md').read_text();rows=[r for r in re.findall(r'^\|\s*([^|*]+?)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|', t, re.M)];tot=re.findall(r'^\|\s*\*\*(\d+) repositories\*\*\s*\|\s*\*\*(\d+)\*\*\s*\|\s*\*\*(\d+)\*\*\s*\|\s*\*\*(\d+)\*\*\s*\|', t, re.M)[0];s=[len(rows)]+[sum(int(r[i]) for r in rows) for i in (1,2,3)];d=s[2]+s[3];pct=round(100*d/s[1]);print('sums', *s, d, '| stated', *[int(x) for x in tot], int(tot[2])+int(tot[3]), '| pct', pct, '| doc says 24%:', '24%' in t)"

claims.claim: `coverage` lists the README numbers no claim mentions and always exits 0 — it is a to-do list, not a gate. Its own report on this README leads with the illustration numbers from the worked example, and the gate still passes.
claims.metric: exit code of `coverage`, and whether it prints candidates
claims.method: the command scans this README, prints every number no claim mentions, and returns 0; only `run` decides pass/fail

claims.claim: Across the 22 repositories this tool guards, `coverage` found 119 number-like mentions matched by a claim and 128 that no claim mentions — an upper bound on unclaimed work, not a defect count.
claims.metric: unclaimed candidates reported by `coverage --max 0` over the 22 guarded repositories
claims.method: run 2026-09-13 against local clones of all 22 repositories, once for each; the figure moves as READMEs change and is dominated by numbers that are not figures at all (example sizes, HTTP codes, CSS percentages, and numbers written as words, which the scan cannot see in either direction)
claims.repro: for d in <the 22 clones>; do python3 -m verify_claims --root ../$d coverage --max 0; done

check.manual: Needs a sibling checkout of all 22 guarded repositories, so it cannot run in this repository's CI. Re-run the loop in `repro` and update the figure here and in docs/measurement.md together; the number is a heuristic backlog, and the document says so.

claims.claim: `docs/index.md` is generated, and its summary line always equals the sum of the rows under it — a hand-edited page would fail this.
claims.metric: rows/claims/machine/manual parsed back out of the committed page
claims.method: `index_page.summarise` re-reads the rendered page: total must equal machine + manual, and the page must still carry the do-not-edit notice
claims.repro: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c "from verify_claims import index_page as i; print(i.summarise(open('docs/index.md').read()))"

check.cmd: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c "from verify_claims import index_page as i;t=open('docs/index.md').read();r,tot,m,man=i.summarise(t);assert tot==m+man,(tot,m,man);assert r>0;assert 'do not edit by hand' in t;print('consistent',r,tot,m,man)"
